Your 6-week journey · 6 weeksView full curriculum ↓
Week 01AI Foundations, Prompt Engineering, APIs & Context Optimization6 sessionsWeek 02MCP, First AI Agent Workflow & Agentic AI Foundations6 sessionsWeek 03No-Code AI Agents, RAG & Production Knowledge Systems6 sessionsWeek 04End-to-End Intelligent Automation, AI UGC Creation & Content Automation6 sessionsWeek 05AI Application Development, Prompt-to-App Building & Integrated AI Systems6 sessionsWeek 06OpenClaw, Production AI Agents, Browser Automation, Security & Enterprise Integrations6 sessions

Overview

Build AI agents and automations that do real work.

A fast-paced 6-week, 36-session program: prompt engineering and APIs, MCP and agentic AI, no-code agents with Dify, n8n, CrewAI and Zapier, production RAG, AI UGC content factories, prompt-to-app development with Lovable, and production agents with OpenClaw.

Starts from AI foundations; most builds are no-code or low-code.

Built for

  • Professionals and founders who want to automate real workflows
  • Marketers and creators scaling content with AI
  • Operations and business teams adopting AI agents
  • Non-coders and developers who want agentic AI fast

Outcomes

What you’ll be able to do.

  1. Engineer reliable prompts and build a reusable library of 20–30 prompts
  2. Optimise tokens, cost and context, and compare models across APIs
  3. Connect AI to tools and data with APIs and the Model Context Protocol (MCP)
  4. Design agent architectures with memory, planning, tools, guardrails and human-in-the-loop control
  5. Build no-code agents and automations in Dify, n8n, CrewAI and Zapier
  6. Ship production-style RAG assistants with citations and conversation memory
  7. Create and automate AI UGC — scripts, avatars, voice and multi-platform video
  8. Build and deploy AI web apps with Lovable, wired to automation workflows via webhooks
  9. Run secure, scheduled production agents with OpenClaw, MCP and Bitwarden

Full curriculum

Every session, day by day.

PDF brochure
Week 01 · Sessions 1–6

AI Foundations, Prompt Engineering, APIs & Context Optimization

Day 1Introduction to AI & Evolution of AI
  • Introduction to AI & Evolution of AI: What is AI, History of AI (Symbolic AI → Machine Learning → Deep Learning → Foundation Models → Generative AI → Agentic AI), AI Timeline (1950–2026), Major AI Paradigms.
  • Key AI Researchers: Alan Turing, John McCarthy, Geoffrey Hinton, Yann LeCun, Yoshua Bengio, Demis Hassabis, Ilya Sutskever.
  • Modern AI Ecosystem: Modern LLM Ecosystem, Open-source vs Proprietary Models, AI Career Opportunities.

Hands-on: AI Foundations Exploration Lab

Explore major stages in the evolution of AI and identify representative technologies/models from each stage. Compare modern open-source and proprietary LLM ecosystems. Students identify potential AI-related career opportunities aligned with their interests and document their initial learning goals for the program.

Deliverables

  • AI Evolution & Timeline Notes
  • Open-source vs Proprietary Model Comparison
  • Personal AI Career/Learning Goal Sheet

Assessment

Understanding of AI evolution, major AI paradigms, modern LLM ecosystem, key contributors to AI, and awareness of AI career opportunities

Day 2Git & GitHub Fundamentals
  • Git & GitHub Fundamentals: What is Git, Why GitHub is important, Repository creation, GitHub profile setup (no commands).
  • LinkedIn Optimization: Personal branding, optimizing profile, creating AI-related posts, building an online presence.
  • Personalized AI Learning Workflow: Using ChatGPT/Claude Custom Instructions to establish a structured AI-assisted learning workflow.

Hands-on: AI Career Setup Lab

Create a GitHub account and first repository, optimize LinkedIn profile, publish the first LinkedIn post about joining the Agentic AI & Automation Program, and build a personalized AI learning workflow using ChatGPT/Claude Custom Instructions.

Deliverables

  • GitHub account + first repository
  • optimized LinkedIn profile
  • first LinkedIn AI post
  • AI learning workflow document

Assessment

GitHub familiarity, professional branding, effective learning-workflow setup, online presence, and participation

Day 3Prompt Engineering Fundamentals
  • Prompt Engineering Fundamentals: Why Prompt Engineering Matters, Prompt Anatomy, Zero-shot, One-shot, Few-shot, Instruction, Role, Persona, Context, Constraint, Goal, Audience, Output, Template Prompting.
  • Structured Prompting: Markdown, JSON, XML, Delimiters, Variables & Placeholders.

Hands-on: Prompt Engineering Lab – Part 1

Build the foundation of a reusable Prompt Library for research, business, coding, content creation, marketing, image generation, and document analysis. Practice converting basic prompts into structured prompts using roles, context, constraints, examples, output specifications, Markdown, JSON, XML, variables, and delimiters.

Deliverables

  • First section of reusable Prompt Library
  • structured-prompt examples across multiple use cases

Assessment

Prompt anatomy, correct selection of prompting techniques, use of structured formats, clarity of instructions, context quality, constraint design, and output control

Day 4Reasoning Prompting
  • Reasoning Prompting: Step-by-Step, Planning, Task Decomposition, Reflection, Critic, Judge, Socratic Prompting (overview), Chain of Draft (CoD).
  • Additional Prompting Applications: Conversational Prompting, Image Prompting, Business & Research Prompting.
  • Whisper Flow AI: Introduction to Whisper Flow AI for prompt workflows.
  • AI Ethics, AI Safety & Hallucinations: Responsible AI usage, hallucination detection, prompt safety, prompt injection awareness.

Hands-on: Prompt Engineering Lab – Part 2

Complete the reusable 20–30 prompt Prompt Library. Use Whisper Flow AI to organize or execute prompt workflows. Test selected prompts across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Perplexity, compare model outputs, identify hallucinations or inconsistencies, and refine prompts for reliability and safety.

Deliverables

  • Completed Prompt Library (20–30 reusable prompts)
  • Prompt Comparison Report
  • Whisper Flow workflow

Assessment

Prompt quality, reasoning and task decomposition, structured prompting, output consistency, responsible AI usage, hallucination awareness, prompt-safety awareness, and ability to compare model behavior

Day 5API Fundamentals
  • API Fundamentals: What is an API, API vs API Key, How APIs Work, REST basics (conceptual), Request & Response, Authentication, Rate Limits, Free AI APIs (Groq, Gemini, OpenRouter, Cohere, Hugging Face, etc.), Integrating APIs into AI applications.
  • Sandbox Environment: What is a Sandbox, Why AI needs Sandboxes, Sandbox vs Local Machine, introduction to ChatGPT Code Interpreter/Python Sandbox.

Hands-on: API & Model Comparison Lab

Generate API keys from available free providers, understand secure handling of API credentials, test the same prompt on multiple models/providers, compare responses, observe rate-limit/model differences, and document how APIs can connect AI models with applications. Demonstrate basic execution inside the ChatGPT Python Sandbox.

Deliverables

  • API keys/configuration setup
  • API Comparison Sheet
  • basic Sandbox demonstration

Assessment

Understanding of APIs and API keys, request/response concepts, authentication, rate limits, model/provider selection, sandbox concepts, and ability to compare AI API outputs

Day 6Token Optimization
  • Token Optimization: Why Token Optimization Matters, Token Counting, Budgeting, Estimation, Cost Analysis, Input & Output Optimization, Prompt Compression, Prompt Simplification, Prompt Rewriting, Instruction Optimization, Minimal Prompting, Delimiter Optimization, Output Constraints, JSON & Markdown Optimization, Few-shot Optimization, Example Selection, Prompt Densification, Chain of Draft (CoD).
  • Introduction to Context Engineering: Context Selection, Context Pruning, Context Summarization.

Hands-on: API, Token & Context Optimization Lab

Estimate token usage and costs for different prompts/models, optimize prompts to reduce token usage without losing required output quality, apply compression/simplification/densification techniques, optimize structured JSON/Markdown outputs, and practice context selection, pruning, and summarization. Use ChatGPT's Python environment to generate practical outputs including CSV, Excel, charts, and PDFs.

Deliverables

  • Token Optimization Report
  • optimized prompt collection
  • completed API Comparison Sheet
  • Sandbox demonstration outputs (CSV / Excel / Chart / PDF)

Assessment

Token efficiency, cost awareness, prompt optimization, output optimization, context-engineering fundamentals, sandbox usage, and ability to maintain output quality while reducing unnecessary token consumption

Week 02 · Sessions 7–12

MCP, First AI Agent Workflow & Agentic AI Foundations

Day 1Model Context Protocol (MCP) — Foundations
  • Model Context Protocol (MCP) — Foundations: Why MCP was created, Problems it solves, MCP Architecture, Clients, Servers, Tools, Resources, Prompts, Transports (STDIO & HTTP), MCP vs APIs, MCP vs Plugins. Introduction to the real-world MCP ecosystem and understanding how MCP standardizes the way AI systems interact with external tools and data sources.

Hands-on: MCP Architecture Exploration Lab

Map the relationship between an MCP Client, MCP Server, Tools, Resources, Prompts, and transport layer. Compare a traditional API-based integration with an MCP-based integration and identify situations where each approach is appropriate. Explore available MCP servers such as Filesystem, Brave Search, GitHub, SQLite, etc.

Deliverables

  • MCP Architecture Diagram
  • MCP vs API Comparison Sheet
  • MCP Component Reference Notes

Assessment

Understanding of MCP purpose, architecture, clients, servers, tools, resources, prompts, transports, MCP vs APIs, MCP vs Plugins, and ability to explain how MCP connects AI systems to external capabilities

Day 2MCP Security & Claude Desktop Integration
  • MCP Security & Claude Desktop Integration: MCP Security, Real-world MCP ecosystem, Enterprise MCP use cases.
  • Claude Desktop + MCP: Installing MCP servers, connecting tools, using MCP with Claude Desktop, understanding how Claude interacts with external systems. Configuration concepts for one or more MCP servers including Filesystem, Brave Search, GitHub, SQLite, etc.

Hands-on: MCP Hands-on Lab

Install Claude Desktop, configure one or more MCP servers, connect external tools/resources, perform searches, read files, interact with connected systems, and complete a small automation using Claude + MCP. Students observe how Claude selects and invokes external tools during a task.

Deliverables

  • Working Claude + MCP setup
  • MCP configuration
  • connected MCP server(s)
  • simple automation workflow

Assessment

MCP concepts, successful setup, tool usage, server configuration, security awareness, workflow understanding, and ability to explain how Claude interacts with external systems through MCP

Day 3Mini Project 1 – Build Your First AI Agent Workflow
  • Mini Project 1 – Build Your First AI Agent Workflow: Project Design & Architecture. Combine Prompt Engineering, APIs, Token Optimization, Sandbox concepts, Claude Desktop, and MCP into a practical automation. Understand how AI agents use tools, context, and workflows to solve real problems. Project planning, problem definition, tool selection, prompt planning, context design, workflow architecture, and MCP-server selection.

Hands-on: Mini Project 1 – Planning & Build Phase

Select one project: Document Research Assistant, Local File Assistant, AI Knowledge Base Assistant, Meeting Notes Analyzer, Personal Productivity Assistant, or Research Automation Workflow. Design the solution and begin building a working AI workflow using Claude Desktop connected to multiple MCP servers, without writing code.

Deliverables

  • Project Problem Statement
  • initial Architecture Diagram
  • MCP Tool/Server Selection
  • Prompt & Workflow Plan
  • partially functional workflow

Assessment

Problem selection, architecture quality, prompt planning, MCP selection, understanding of tools/context/workflows, and practical workflow-design approach

Day 4Mini Project 1 – Build Your First AI Agent Workflow
  • Mini Project 1 – Build Your First AI Agent Workflow: Integration, Testing & Presentation. Integrate prompts, tools, multiple MCP servers, context, API concepts where applicable, token-efficient instructions, and workflow logic into a complete automation. Testing, refinement, troubleshooting, documentation, demonstration, and evaluation. Brief Introduction to Multi-Agent Thinking as preparation for the next stage of the program.

Hands-on: Mini Project 1 – Completion Lab

Complete the selected AI workflow. Test different inputs and edge cases, refine prompts and tool usage, validate MCP integrations, document the architecture and workflow, and prepare a demonstration video or live presentation explaining how the system solves the selected problem.

Deliverables

  • Functional AI workflow
  • Architecture Diagram
  • demonstration video/live presentation
  • documentation

Assessment

Workflow design, MCP usage, prompt quality, tool integration, problem-solving approach, presentation, documentation quality, successful end-to-end execution, and readiness to progress from simple workflows toward agentic systems

Day 5Introduction to Agentic AI
  • Introduction to Agentic AI: From Generative AI to Agentic AI, Generative AI vs Traditional AI, Generative AI vs Agentic AI, What is an AI Agent?, Characteristics of AI Agents, AI Assistant vs AI Copilot vs AI Agent, Why Agentic AI is the Next Evolution, Real-world Agentic AI Applications.
  • Core Principles of Agentic AI: Goal-Oriented Behavior, Autonomy, Agency, Proactiveness, Reactiveness, Decision Making, Adaptability, Context Awareness, Environmental Awareness, Human-in-the-Loop (HITL), Human-on-the-Loop, Human-out-of-the-Loop.
  • How an AI Agent Thinks: Perception, Observation, Planning, Reasoning, Execution, Reflection, Self-Correction, Feedback Loop, Agent Loop: Observe → Think → Plan → Act → Reflect, Goal Decomposition, Task Decomposition, Iterative Execution.

Hands-on: Agent Design Workshop – Part 1

Select a real-world business problem such as Customer Support, HR Assistant, Research Assistant, Sales Assistant, Personal Productivity, etc. Define the agent's purpose, goals, environment, inputs, outputs, degree of autonomy, human oversight requirements, major tasks, decision points, and agent loop. Begin the architecture in Whimsical, FigJam, or Miro.

Deliverables

  • Agent Problem Definition
  • Goals & Task Decomposition Sheet
  • Agent Loop Diagram
  • Human-Oversight Strategy
  • initial Agent Architecture Diagram

Assessment

Understanding of Agentic AI concepts, difference between assistants/copilots/agents, autonomy and agency, agent-loop reasoning, goal decomposition, task decomposition, HITL concepts, and applicability to a real-world problem

Day 6Context & Memory
  • Context & Memory: Context, Context Window, User Context, Session Context, Task Context, Short-Term Memory, Long-Term Memory, Working Memory, Persistent Memory.
  • Agent Architecture: Brain (LLM), Planner, Memory, Executor, Tools, Environment, Inputs & Outputs.
  • Agent Collaboration: Single-Agent vs Multi-Agent Systems, Agent Roles, Delegation, Collaboration, Orchestration.
  • Reliability & Safety: Guardrails, Validation, Monitoring, Logging, Explainability, Trustworthy AI.
  • Automation Concepts: Workflow vs Agent, Rule-Based Automation vs AI Agents, Event-Driven Automation, Trigger vs Goal, Future of AI Automation.

Hands-on: Agent Design Workshop – Part 2

Complete the AI-agent architecture begun on Day 5. Define the agent's LLM/Brain, Planner, Memory, Executor, Tools, Environment, Inputs, Outputs, workflow, reasoning structure and interactions. Determine whether the solution should use a single agent or multiple agents, define delegation/orchestration where applicable, and add guardrails, validation, monitoring and logging. Finalize the architecture using Whimsical, FigJam, or Miro and present the design.

Deliverables

  • Complete AI Agent Architecture Diagram
  • Agent Workflow Document
  • Tool Selection Sheet
  • Agent Design Presentation

Assessment

Understanding of context and memory, architecture design, reasoning flow, agent decomposition, workflow logic, tool selection, single-agent vs multi-agent design, delegation/orchestration, reliability and safety considerations, automation concepts, and presentation quality

Week 03 · Sessions 13–18

No-Code AI Agents, RAG & Production Knowledge Systems

Day 1No-Code AI Agent Platforms — Foundations & Comparison
  • No-Code AI Agent Platforms — Foundations & Comparison: Introduction to Dify, n8n, CrewAI, and Zapier.
  • Platform comparison, strengths, limitations, and common components: Triggers, Nodes, Agents, Tools, Knowledge Bases, Variables, Workflows. Understanding AI workflow builders, agent orchestration, integrations, automation patterns, and business use cases. Introduction to how different platforms solve the same automation problem using different approaches.

Hands-on: AI Automation Lab – Part 1

Explore and compare Dify, n8n, CrewAI, and Zapier. Map the core components of each platform and identify how triggers, nodes, agents, tools, knowledge bases, variables, and workflows are represented. Build the first two simple automations: (1) Dify AI Chatbot and (2) n8n AI Workflow.

Deliverables

  • Working Dify AI Chatbot
  • working n8n AI Workflow
  • initial Platform Comparison Sheet
  • workflow screenshots

Assessment

Platform understanding, identification of common workflow components, basic workflow creation, automation logic, integration concepts, and ability to compare platform approaches

Day 2No-Code Agent Orchestration & Automation Patterns
  • No-Code Agent Orchestration & Automation Patterns: Deeper comparison of Dify, n8n, CrewAI, and Zapier for automation, reasoning, integrations, and agent orchestration. Understanding when to use workflow automation versus agent-based orchestration, how platforms structure sequential tasks, external integrations, and business automation patterns.

Hands-on: AI Automation Lab – Part 2

Build the remaining two original automations: (3) CrewAI Multi-Agent Workflow and (4) Zapier AI Automation. Compare all four platforms by recreating or analyzing a similar automation objective across them. Evaluate how each platform handles automation, reasoning, integrations, and orchestration.

Deliverables

  • Four working automation workflows in total
  • completed Platform Comparison Report
  • Workflow Screenshots

Assessment

Workflow creation, automation logic, tool and platform selection, agent orchestration understanding, comparison and analysis, and ability to explain strengths and limitations of each platform

Day 3Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) — Foundations
  • Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) — Foundations: What is RAG?, Why LLMs Hallucinate, LLM Knowledge vs External Knowledge, Fine-tuning vs RAG, RAG Architecture & Pipeline, Retrieval Pipeline, Generation Pipeline.
  • Document Ingestion: OCR, Text Extraction, PDF Parsing, Metadata, Data Cleaning.
  • Chunking Fundamentals: Chunking, Chunk Size, Chunk Overlap, Recursive Chunking, Semantic Chunking.

Hands-on: Basic RAG Lab – Part 1

Build the conceptual RAG pipeline and begin simple document-based AI assistants. Upload documents, create knowledge bases, ingest PDFs, inspect extracted text and metadata, experiment with chunk size and overlap, and test basic document Q&A. Begin implementations in Dify and n8n.

Deliverables

  • Initial RAG Pipeline Diagram
  • two basic document-based RAG applications
  • document-ingestion and chunking notes

Assessment

Understanding of RAG concepts, hallucination mitigation, fine-tuning vs RAG, document ingestion, OCR/text extraction, metadata, data cleaning, chunking, chunk size, chunk overlap, and overall retrieval/generation flow

Day 4RAG Retrieval Mechanics & Modern RAG
  • RAG Retrieval Mechanics & Modern RAG: Embeddings, Embedding Models, Embedding Similarity, Cosine Similarity, Vector Databases (ChromaDB, Pinecone, Weaviate, Qdrant, FAISS), Retrieval, Semantic Search vs Keyword Search, Hybrid Retrieval, Top-K Retrieval, Context Injection, Prompt Augmentation, Grounded Generation, Source Citations.
  • Introduction to Modern RAG: Agentic RAG, Graph RAG, Multimodal RAG, SQL RAG, Code RAG, API RAG.

Hands-on: Basic RAG Lab – Part 2

Complete simple document-based AI assistants using Dify, n8n, CrewAI, and Zapier. Ask questions from PDFs, compare retrieval quality and grounded responses, inspect how each platform handles knowledge bases and retrieval, and observe the effect of chunking and retrieval settings. Complete the platform comparison of RAG implementations.

Deliverables

  • Four basic RAG applications
  • completed RAG Pipeline Diagram
  • Platform Comparison Report

Assessment

Embeddings, retrieval flow, vector database concepts, semantic vs keyword search, hybrid retrieval, Top-K, context injection, grounded generation, source citations, practical implementation, retrieval quality, and comparison of platforms

FAQ

About AI Agents.

Have a question that isn’t covered here? Ask an advisor directly.

Ask on WhatsApp
Do I need to know how to code?

No heavy coding is required. Most builds use no-code and low-code platforms such as Claude Desktop with MCP, Dify, n8n, CrewAI, Zapier and Lovable, with JSON, APIs and webhooks explained from first principles.

What will I have built by the end?

A prompt library, an MCP-powered agent workflow, four platform automations, a production-style RAG assistant, an intelligent automation system, an AI UGC content factory, an AI web app, an app-plus-automation integration and a production OpenClaw agent.

What is MCP and why does it matter?

The Model Context Protocol standardises how AI systems connect to tools and data. You will learn its architecture — clients, servers, tools, resources, prompts and transports — and use it with Claude Desktop and OpenClaw.

Is AI-generated content covered responsibly?

Yes. The UGC weeks include ethics, AI disclosure, copyright and commercial rights, and every agent build covers guardrails, validation and human oversight.

Is it suitable for business owners?

Absolutely — every project is framed around real business use cases: customer support, research, lead qualification, internal knowledge, content and operations.
